validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. This segment is Phase 5 of the well-documented six-phase 'Upper Egypt/South Valley Gas Pipeline' (Dahshur-Aswan trunk), built by Petrojet for Nile Valley Gas Co (NVGC), inaugurated by Mubarak Dec 30 2010/Jan 3 2011. Confirmed via the sheet's own cited Arabic ref (almasryalyoum.com, 200 OK) AND two independent English trade sources found this pass: pipeliner.com.au ('Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline reaches Sohag', Australian Pipeliner, 23 Sep 2009, 200 OK) and petroleumafrica.com ('Mubarak Inaugurates Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline', 200 OK). CLASSIFICATION: correct - national gas transmission trunk, not gathering/plant-internal. DUPLICATE: none. GEM has segmented this trunk into six sequential ProjectIDs (P6697 Dahshur-Karema, P6698 Karema-BeniSuef, P6699 BeniSuef-AbuQurqas, P6700 AbuQurqas-Asyut, P6701 Asyut-Girga, P6702 Girga-Aswan) that map 1:1, in order and length, onto almasryalyoum's own six numbered phases (90/30/150/147/121/390 km, summing to the article's stated 930 km total). P6701 = phase 5 exactly, no overlap with P6700 or P6702. GulfPub also carries a matching six-segment South Valley Gas Pipeline family (its own Asyut->Gerga entry, dia 32in, op=Nile Valley Gas Company) rather than one merged row, corroborating the six-way split. ATTRIBUTION: current Owner1=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS) 100% is plausible as ultimate state owner, but pipeliner (2009) says Petrojet built the line 'for the Nile Valley Gas Company', and GulfPub independently lists operator = Nile Valley Gas Company for this same pipeline family. NVGC's other public profile (egyptoil-gas.com) is as an Upper-Egypt gas *distribution* company (household connections, Beni Suef), a subsidiary of TAQA Gas -- so NVGC's exact role (transmission owner/operator vs. downstream distributor) is ambiguous from open sources; recommend a human check whether NVGC belongs alongside/instead of EGAS as Owner or Operator, but not changing Owner1 on this pass (EGAS as state trunk-line owner is defensible and unrebutted).

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC conflict on length/diameter for this specific leg, across otherwise-solid independent sources: (1) almasryalyoum (GEM's own cited ref, Arabic, precise quote: 'المرحلة الخامسة من أسيوط تطي جرجا بطول 121 كم وقطر 32 بوصة' = 'phase 5, Assiut to Girga, 121 km, 32-inch diameter') matches GEM exactly (121 km / 32 in). (2) pipeliner.com.au (Sep 2009, independent English trade press) instead describes 'Stage four... 100 km of 30 inch diameter pipeline from Assiut to Sohag' -- different length (100 vs 121 km), different diameter (30 vs 32 in), and a different named endpoint (Sohag vs Girga; Girga is ~26 km further south of Sohag city along the same corridor, so the pipeliner figure plausibly describes an earlier construction-progress milestone (reaching Sohag) rather than the final as-built endpoint at Girga -- a defensible but unconfirmed reconciliation). (3) petroleumafrica.com independently corroborates pipeliner's framing, also naming the leg 'Assiut to Sohag (100 km)' with no mention of Girga at all. (4) GulfPub's independent scrape carries yet a third figure for its 'Asyut -> Gerga' entry: 75 km, 32 in (diameter agrees with GEM/almasryalyoum; length disagrees with all three other sources). Net: diameter 32in has 2 independent supports (almasryalyoum + GulfPub) vs 1 conflicting (pipeliner 30in) -> keep, medium-high tier. Length has THREE disagreeing independent figures (75 / 100 / 121 km) and only the sheet's own single Arabic ref supports the current GEM value of 121 -- this does not meet the 2-independent-agree bar. Recommend a human note; not overwriting without stronger consensus.

Single-source pairing only (see spec concern above re: two independent English sources giving 100 km and 75 km for what may be the same or a shorter-scoped leg) -- filled to remove the orphan-ref gap, tier kept at medium/single-source rather than claiming 2-independent corroboration.

Endpoints Asyut->Girga (Girga sits in Sohag governorate, matching EndState/Province='Sohag') are stated verbatim in the primary source and independently consistent with pipeliner/petroleumafrica's 'Assiut to Sohag' framing of the same leg (Girga is ~26km further south along the same corridor from Sohag city).

routes.corridor_desc: The line runs the Nile Valley trunk corridor southward from Asyut, through Sohag Governorate, to Girga (~26 km south of Sohag city). Sohag city is included as a sourced waypoint because an independent 2009 trade-press account (pipeliner.com.au) describes this same construction stage as having 'reached Sohag' before the phase's final documented endpoint at Girga (almasryalyoum, 2010) -- consistent with the line passing at or very near Sohag en route to Girga. No source gives intermediate route geometry (river-bank side, exact alignment relative to the Nile, road/rail paralleling), so this is an endpoint-level corridor bound only, not a traced route.
routes.researcher_notes: Start/end city coordinates are standard geocodes for named places (Asyut, Girga, Sohag), not fabricated; no pipeline-specific route line or waypoint list was located in any source. Suggested accuracy is 'low' (named endpoints only, real corridor direction established, but no actual traced alignment) rather than 'medium' or 'high'.

summary: P6701 (South Valley Gas Pipeline, Asyut-Girga phase) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate (1:1 with phase 5 of the sheet's own cited six-phase source, mirrored by GEM's own P6697-P6702 split and by GulfPub's parallel six-segment family); flagged a genuine spec conflict (length 121km GEM/almasryalyoum vs 100km pipeliner/petroleumafrica vs 75km GulfPub, diameter 32in vs one conflicting 30in source) and a lesser owner/operator caveat (EGAS vs Nile Valley Gas Co); paired the existing Length and Location values with the sheet's own verified primary ref.
